cohort: Pregnant women admitted to the Obstetrics Service of a tertiary reference maternity hospital in Northeastern Brazil, with 72 cases of fetal death and 144 controls (live births)
finding: Gestations with fetal death are more prone to delays in obstetric care, including fewer prenatal consultations, less risk classification of pregnancy, and inadequate guidance about the delivery location, despite having a higher frequency of obstetric complications.
mod_finding: The study found a lower frequency of Cesarean sections in the fetal death group compared to the live birth group.
gest_age: Approximately matched between cases and controls
